heading_path: Buyer's Guide Determine the solicitation period - Figure 1: Normal minimum solicitation period
blocks.markdown: Normal minimum solicitation periods Regardless of minimum solicitation period requirements, offerors must always be given enough time to prepare and submit compliant offers. The following must be considered when determining the solicitation period for a procurement: the nature and complexity of the procurement the extent of subcontracting anticipated the time necessary for transmitting tenders by non-electronic means Minimum solicitation periods for procurements Procurement type Normal minimum solicitation period No trade agreement—Low dollar value May be less than 15 calendar days for efficiency and cost effectiveness: Goods: below $25K (including taxes) Construction: below $40K (including taxes) Services: below $40K (including taxes) No trade agreement—Not low dollar value 15 calendar days Canadian Free Trade Agreement only 15 calendar days One or more international trade agreements—Commercial goods and/or services 15 calendar days if the Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) and tender documents are published at the same time electronically 13 calendar days if 15 calendar days is impracticable 10 calendar days if offers are accepted electronically Note: If the NPP and tender documents are not published at the same time electronically, the guidance for non-commercial goods and/or services below applies. One or more international trade agreements—Non-commercial goods and/or services 40 calendar days, which can be reduced by 5 days, to no less than 25 days, for each of the following conditions: the NPP is published electronically all tender documents are available electronically from the NPP date of publication the procuring entity accepts tenders electronically Note: If using limited tendering, the solicitation period should be at least 15 calendar days.

blocks.markdown:
| Procurement type | Normal minimum solicitation period |

| Canadian Free Trade Agreement only | 15 calendar days |
